name: h_inner_vs_left_between
left: SELECT a.id, b.y FROM a JOIN b ON a.k = b.k WHERE b.y BETWEEN 1 AND 2
right: SELECT a.id, b.y FROM b RIGHT JOIN a ON a.k = b.k WHERE b.y BETWEEN 1 AND 2
why: b RIGHT JOIN a is a LEFT JOIN b; BETWEEN rejects null-extended b rows.

name: h_comma_three_vs_left
left: SELECT a.id, c.z FROM a, b, c WHERE a.k = b.k AND b.id = c.k
right: SELECT a.id, c.z FROM a LEFT JOIN b ON a.k = b.k LEFT JOIN c ON b.id = c.k WHERE c.k IS NOT NULL
why: c.k IS NOT NULL rejects c, and c can only match through b.

name: h_anti_two_keys
left: SELECT a.id FROM a LEFT JOIN b ON a.k = b.k AND a.x = b.y WHERE b.k IS NULL
right: SELECT a.id FROM a WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM b WHERE b.k = a.k AND b.y = a.x)
why: b.k IS NULL holds exactly on null-extended rows; the whole ON moves into NOT EXISTS.

name: h_semi_distinct_in
left: SELECT DISTINCT a.x FROM a LEFT JOIN b ON b.k = a.k WHERE b.y IS NOT NULL
right: SELECT DISTINCT a.x FROM a WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM b WHERE b.k = a.k AND b.y IS NOT NULL)
why: DISTINCT over a semi join with the WHERE test inside EXISTS.

name: h_full_both_is_not_null
left: SELECT a.id, b.id AS bid FROM a FULL JOIN b ON a.k = b.k WHERE a.id IS NOT NULL AND b.id IS NOT NULL
right: SELECT a.id, b.id AS bid FROM a JOIN b ON a.k = b.k WHERE a.id IS NOT NULL AND b.id IS NOT NULL
why: a.id IS NOT NULL and b.id IS NOT NULL reject both kinds of null-extended row; matched rows with a NULL id are dropped on both sides.

name: h_fk_three
left: SELECT c.id, a.x, b.y FROM c JOIN a ON c.k = a.id JOIN b ON a.k = b.id
right: SELECT c.id, a.x, b.y FROM c JOIN a ON c.k = a.id LEFT JOIN b ON b.id = a.k
why: a comes in through an inner join and a.k is a NOT NULL foreign key to b.id.

name: h_having_max
left: SELECT a.k, MAX(b.y) AS m FROM a LEFT JOIN b ON a.k = b.k GROUP BY a.k HAVING MAX(b.y) >= 0
right: SELECT a.k, MAX(b.y) AS m FROM a JOIN b ON a.k = b.k GROUP BY a.k HAVING MAX(b.y) >= 0
why: MAX(b.y) >= 0 is NULL for groups with no match, and MAX skips null-extended rows.

name: h_in_subquery_right
left: SELECT a.id, b.y FROM a JOIN b ON a.k = b.k WHERE a.x IN (SELECT z FROM c)
right: SELECT a.id, b.y FROM a RIGHT JOIN b ON a.k = b.k WHERE a.x IN (SELECT z FROM c)
why: a.x IN (subquery) rejects rows where a is null-extended.

name: h_cross_count_where
left: SELECT a.id, t.n FROM a CROSS JOIN (SELECT COUNT(b.y) AS n FROM b WHERE b.y > 1) AS t
right: SELECT a.id, t.n FROM a LEFT JOIN (SELECT COUNT(b.y) AS n FROM b WHERE b.y > 1) AS t ON TRUE
why: An aggregate without GROUP BY returns exactly one row.

name: h_nested_right
left: SELECT b.y, c.z FROM b JOIN c ON b.id = c.k RIGHT JOIN a ON a.k = b.k
right: SELECT b.y, c.z FROM a LEFT JOIN (b JOIN c ON b.id = c.k) ON a.k = b.k
why: b JOIN c RIGHT JOIN a is a LEFT JOIN (b JOIN c).

name: h_ne_anti_or
left: SELECT a.id FROM a LEFT JOIN b ON a.k = b.k OR a.x = b.y WHERE b.k IS NULL
right: SELECT a.id FROM a WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM b WHERE b.k = a.k)
why: With OR in the ON, b.k IS NULL can also hold on a matched row (matched through a.x = b.y).

name: h_ne_full_one_side
left: SELECT a.id, b.y FROM a FULL JOIN b ON a.k = b.k WHERE b.y > 0
right: SELECT a.id, b.y FROM a LEFT JOIN b ON a.k = b.k WHERE b.y > 0
why: b.y > 0 keeps unmatched b rows, which only the FULL JOIN has.

name: h_ne_having_sum_ge_null
left: SELECT a.id, SUM(b.y) AS s FROM a LEFT JOIN b ON a.k = b.k GROUP BY a.id HAVING COUNT(*) > 0
right: SELECT a.id, SUM(b.y) AS s FROM a JOIN b ON a.k = b.k GROUP BY a.id

name: h_ne_fk_on_parent_nonkey
left: SELECT a.id, b.y FROM a JOIN b ON a.k = b.id AND a.x = b.k
right: SELECT a.id, b.y FROM a LEFT JOIN b ON a.k = b.id AND a.x = b.k
why: The extra ON test can fail for the parent row.

name: h_ne_cross_vs_left_where_nullable
left: SELECT a.id, b.y FROM a CROSS JOIN b
right: SELECT a.id, b.y FROM a LEFT JOIN b ON TRUE WHERE b.y IS NOT NULL
why: b.y IS NOT NULL also drops real rows whose b.y is NULL.

name: h_ne_semi_bag
left: SELECT a.x FROM a JOIN b ON a.k = b.k
right: SELECT a.x FROM a WHERE a.k IN (SELECT k FROM b)
why: A join repeats an a row once per match; IN does not.
